cars.bio: a plain family saloon that a few mechanics turned into a giant killer. light, honest and happy to slide on a lifted throttle.
tiny wheels, tiny car, enormous grin. it understeers into hairpins and claws its way back out of them.
a wedge built for one job. short, nervous and brilliant, it steers with the throttle as much as the wheel.
wings, vents and a five-cylinder howl. wait for the turbo, then hang on: the fastest thing on a gravel road.
the sensible one. grip everywhere, a gearbox that never misses, and a boxer burble that carries through the trees.
